corrections.was: The CPU column fills in. CPUParticles2D and its 3D twin are simulated on the CPU, the processor. They run on a wider range of hardware but handle fewer particles. The CPU node has only one of the five, emission shape. Its cost rises with every particle. In one measured run, one thousand cost zero point zero three five milliseconds a frame, and fifty thousand cost one point six one. For example, the coin burst in the Walker 3D platformer uses the 3D CPU node.

corrections.why: The 0.035 ms and 1.61 ms figures are not one run: Chapter 9 reports the mean of three fresh-process runs (headless, --fixed-fps 60) on the instructor's single Mac, so 'one measured run' misstates the measurement; 'measured on one machine' is what the chapter supports.

corrections.was: Explosion radius over time, grown two ways. A Timing curve varies how fast an effect grows and slows, instead of using a constant rate. The grey line grows at a steady rate. The red one starts fast and then slows. At forty percent of the time, the steady one has reached forty percent of its size and the eased one seventy-eight. For example, a grenade blast in your game that bursts out quickly and then settles feels powerful, while a steady growth feels flat.

corrections.why: Spoken without a pause, 'the eased one seventy-eight' is heard as one hundred seventy-eight; the slide says eased 78% of size, so a comma keeps the number right by ear.

corrections.was: I want a burst, not a stream becomes, set explosiveness to one and one shot to true, with amount thirty-two. With explosiveness zero the births come in small batches. With explosiveness one, all thirty-two come in the first tenth of a second.
corrections.now: I want a burst, not a stream becomes, set explosiveness to one and one shot to true, with amount thirty-two. With explosiveness zero the births spread out evenly, a few in each tenth of a second. With explosiveness one, all thirty-two come in the first tenth of a second.
corrections.why: Explosiveness zero spreads births evenly across the cycle (Chapter 9 timing model; slide 4 entry); 'small batches' describes the chart's 0.1 s bins, not the setting, and suggests clumped emission.
